title: Xi'an's 13.74 km Wall or Nanjing's Signed Bricks? | China Travel Expert
description:
Two Ming city walls, two reasons to go — which one do you walk?

Xi'an's Ming city wall is a complete rectangular loop of 13.74 km, built from 1370 to 1378 under the Hongwu Emperor. It is one of the best-preserved ancient city walls in China, and you can walk or cycle the full circuit right on top of the ramparts.

Nanjing's Ming city wall is famous for a different reason: its bricks were a quality-control system. Many are stamped with Chinese characters recording where the brick came from, the official in charge of making it, and the individual maker — so a faulty brick could be traced straight back to the people responsible.

🧭 Expert Tip: in Nanjing, start at Zhonghua Gate (Zhonghuamen), the grandest Ming fortress gate; in Xi'an, rent a bike at the South Gate to ride the whole 13.74 km loop.

西安明城墙是一个 13.74 公里的完整闭环，1370–1378 年修建，可以步行或骑行走完全程；南京明城墙的城砖上刻有产地、管工官员和工匠的名字，是古代的质量追责制。
